structured.approach: I used the data-science-steps skill (DS-02) for the procedure, then read feat.tasks through context_get (receipt b0fd4d2) to find the two Data Science tasks for ap_forecast, TSK-03 and TSK-04. org.permission_table is restricted, so I used it only through the tool:repo-access view, which says no secrets are required or granted for ap_forecast. To check that against the code, I searched the ap_forecast checkout case-insensitively for environment-variable, key, token, secret and password patterns. I also read explain.py, models.json and ci.py. The only matches were the model setting max_tokens. explain.py only builds the request dict and sends nothing, and CI runs locally with no credentials. Both the required set and the granted set are empty, so I raised no access request. A shared-memory search showed that BE-02 reached the same result for ap_aging. I did not use the verifier because the output makes few factual statements and each is cited to a file I read.

claims.text: The Data Science lane has two tasks in ap_forecast: TSK-03 (STORY-03, rule-based vendor_risk, no LLM, no network, no models.json read) and TSK-04 (STORY-04, the risk=None parameter on build_explanation_request).
The permission table grants no secrets for ap_forecast and says none are required.
build_explanation_request only builds a dict with provider, model, max_tokens and messages from config or load_config(), and makes no network call.
models.json names provider acme-llm and model acme-text-2 with max_tokens 300, and holds no credential.
CI runs locally (compile, unittest, coverage with COVERAGE_MIN 90.0, AST static checks) and needs no credentials.
Nothing new calls build_explanation_request with risk, and sending the label to acme-llm waits on Architect confirmation TQ-8, which gates release, not coding.
The required secrets and the granted secrets are both empty in every environment, so no access request is raised and no excess access needs revoking.

open_questions: SSQ-1 (non-blocking): If an acme-llm request is ever sent at run time, which runtime owns the provider credential and its permission-table entry? ap_forecast only builds the request, and sending is gated by TQ-8.
structured.summary: I wrote task.secrets_scope for FEAT-ZD-48600. TSK-03 and TSK-04 in ap_forecast need no secrets in any environment, and the permission table grants none. A search of the code found no reads of environment variables, keys or tokens, so there is no gap and I raised no access request. One non-blocking question asks who would own an acme-llm credential if the explanation request were ever sent; that is outside this task.
